```
  Dimensions:        1,536        Avg query:    18ms
  Last VACUUM:       2h ago       Index type:   ivfflat

  [Run VACUUM]   [View Index Stats]
```

**Section C — Storage Browser (S3)**
Simple 2-panel file browser:
- Left: folder tree (`/profiles/`, `/cvs/`, `/transcripts/`, `/exports/`)
- Right: file list with name, size, last modified, `[Copy URL]` action

---

## ⚙️ Technical Constraints

- **Framework**: React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS
- **Component style**: Match FarmUI — functional, unstyled-base components with explicit Tailwind utility classes. No component library wrappers (no ShadCN magic, no MUI).
- **State**: Local state for drawers/modals. No Redux needed at design stage.
- **Tables**: Custom `<table>` with Tailwind — not DataTable libraries. Zebra striping via `odd:bg-zinc-900`.
- **Responsive**: Design for `min-width: 1280px`. This is an admin tool, not a mobile app.
- **Font stack**: `'IBM Plex Mono', monospace` for data values. `'DM Sans', sans-serif` for UI labels. Load via Google Fonts.

---

## 🚫 Explicitly Forbidden

- ❌ Gradients (no `bg-gradient-*`)
- ❌ Glassmorphism / `backdrop-blur`
- ❌ Rounded corners larger than `rounded-md`
- ❌ Drop shadows beyond `shadow-sm`
- ❌ Purple, blue, or indigo accent colors
- ❌ Animated loaders / spinners except a simple CSS border-spin
- ❌ Illustration or decorative imagery
- ❌ Chart tooltips with heavy styling
- ❌ Modal overlays for simple actions — use inline drawers or confirm banners

---

## ✅ Key Interaction Patterns

- **User row click** → right drawer slides in (not a modal)
- **"Retry" buttons** → inline spinner replaces button text, then success/fail state
- **Force Logout** → confirm inline (`Are you sure? [Confirm] [Cancel]` inline below the button, not a modal)
- **Broadcast send** → disabled until Subject + Body filled; recipient count updates live as role filters change
- **Airflow table rows** → "Open in Airflow ↗" opens in a new tab (not embedded iframe)
- **Knowledge chunk edit** → warn banner appears on first keystroke, Save button activates

---

CARDS

Padding: 16px–20px

CLEANUP

- Remove excess spacing

- Calm  
- Structured

Hover feels responsive  
Layout feels intentional  

--------------------------------------------------

- Spacing  
- Animation  
- UI

items.title: Copy Preservation
items.description: Preserves original copy exactly. May add clearly labeled missing support content, but never removes, rewrites, shortens, or invents facts.
items.prompt:
Preserve the original copy exactly as provided.

Non-negotiable rules:

1. Do not rewrite the user’s original copy.
2. Do not shorten, paraphrase, simplify, polish, or reword existing copy.
3. Do not remove any sentence, phrase, bullet point, CTA, disclaimer, heading, subheading, label, or section.
4. Do not exclude copy for brevity, layout convenience, or design preference.
5. Do not “improve” tone, wording, or clarity unless the user explicitly asks for copywriting changes.
6. If copy is too long for a layout, adjust the design, spacing, typography, or section structure instead of changing the copy.
7. If content is missing and the page clearly needs a support element, you may add only the missing structural content, such as:
   - FAQ questions
   - placeholder labels
   - section dividers
   - button labels already implied by the page
   - CMS field placeholders
8. Any added content must be clearly marked as added support content and must not replace original copy.
9. Never invent or generate statistics, percentages, rankings, research claims, or outcomes unless they were explicitly provided by the user.
10. Never fabricate credentials, insurance claims, accreditations, research backing, dates, locations, or performance data.
11. If a fact is missing, leave it blank, label it as a placeholder, or ask for it rather than inventing it.
12. Maintain all original headings, section order, bullets, CTAs, and key phrases unless the user explicitly requests restructuring.
13. Keep the original message, tone, and wording intact.
14. When in doubt, preserve rather than change.

Priority order:
1. Preserve original copy
2. Preserve factual accuracy
3. Preserve section hierarchy
4. Improve layout without editing text

Design behavior:
- Solve overflow with spacing, layout changes, card resizing, typography adjustments, containers, or section expansion
- Do not solve layout problems by cutting or rewriting text
- Keep CTAs exactly as written
- Keep pillar order, framework order, and branded language exactly as provided

If support content must be added, use this label:
[Added support content]

Examples:
- Allowed: adding FAQ placeholders if the user requested an FAQ section but did not provide questions
- Allowed: adding “Image placeholder” or “CMS content block” labels
- Not allowed: rewriting a paragraph to be shorter
- Not allowed: replacing original bullets with summarized bullets
- Not allowed: inventing data or claims to make the page sound stronger

Final rule:
Original copy is the source of truth. Protect it.

items.title: Video Generation / UI Fly-Through
items.description: Cinematic camera motion over the user's own draft screenshot - floating device, perspective push, desk scene - for launch posts and teasers. Camera-only discipline keeps the video model from redrawing the interface: the design is composited into a plate first, then animated with one modest move and a locked-UI clause. Adapted from rediumvex's ai-video-generator-claude and Krea's krea-marketing (both MIT).
items.prompt:
# UI Fly-Through

Generative video wants to redraw your interface; this skill is about never letting it. The deliverable is cinematic camera motion over the user's own design - a r3xdec design draft screenshot placed into a scene and flown past, orbited, or pushed toward - for launch posts and teasers. The design already exists and is already right. The video's only job is to add depth, light, and a camera; the moment it is allowed to touch the interface itself, every label it redraws comes back wrong.

`Video Generation / Billboard Placement` warns that video models fight UI screenshots. That warning stands. This skill is the disciplined exception, and it holds only inside strict limits: the camera moves, the interface does not, and nobody is asked to read anything.

## When to use

- A finished draft needs a launch or teaser asset that shows the actual product, not an abstraction.
- A social post wants the interface with depth and polish - a floating device, a lit desk, a slow push.
- The user asks for a "product video", "app showcase", or "demo clip" where the motion is atmosphere, not instruction.

Do not use for: a walkthrough the viewer must read or follow (record the real screen; generative video cannot hold legible small text through a scene change), the brand mark placed in the world (use `Video Generation / Billboard Placement`), an ambient background behind a headline (use `Video Generation / Hero Loop`), or in-product UI motion (that belongs in CSS, not in a video file).

## Why camera-only is the whole trick

Rendered text survives a camera move and dies in a scene change. This is a verified behavior, not a preference: a frame containing dense real text, animated with a pure camera-only move and the instruction that nothing else changes, stays legible through the last frame - while the same frame under motion that alters the scene (elements animating, objects entering, light shifting) drifts progressively, and the drift lands on the smallest type first.

So the discipline is absolute:

- **Never ask the UI to be alive.** No "data flows", no "charts animate", no "notifications slide in", no cursor, no scrolling, no screen transitions. Each of those is an instruction to redraw the interface, and a redrawn interface is a deformed one.
- **One camera move per clip**, modest and complete: an orbit of `10–15°`, a push that covers a fraction of the frame, a lateral drift. No whip pans, no fast zooms, no move that becomes another move.
- **Accept what the shot is.** Small text reads as texture at these sizes; the clip sells depth, materiality, and confidence. If the brief needs the viewer to read the interface, this is the wrong tool.
- **The UI stays sharpest inside a scene.** A screenshot filling the frame edge-to-edge gives the model nothing to do except reinterpret pixels. A screen at `50–70%` of frame, angled in an environment, gives the camera something real to move through and keeps the interface a photographed object rather than a canvas.

## Shot menu

Pick one and commit.

| Shot | What moves | What stays locked | Reads as |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Floating device** - the design on a slab or laptop at a slight angle in a dark void, rim-lit, soft reflection below | Camera orbits `10–15°`, shallow depth of field | Device position, screen content, light setup | Premium, product-first |
| **Perspective push** - camera pushes toward the screen plane, stopping just before it fills the frame | Camera travels forward at constant speed | Screen content, framing endpoint chosen so UI never goes edge-to-edge | Confident, immersive |
| **Desk scene** - device in a real workspace at dusk, warm ambient light, props in bokeh | Camera drifts laterally or pushes gently | Screen content, environment layout | Credible, human-scale |
| **Side glide** - two or three screens of the same design system in an angled row | Camera dollies along the row with parallax | Every screen's content, the row's geometry | System-level, "this is a whole product" |

The perspective push is the highest-risk shot: the closer the screen gets to filling the frame, the more the model is tempted to reinterpret it. End the move with visible scene around the screen.

## Two stages, always

The same plate-then-animate doctrine as `Video Generation / Billboard Placement`: there is a still in between, and the composition is won there.

**Stage 1 - build the plate with image generation.** Attach the actual draft screenshot as a reference image and generate the scene around it: the device slab, the desk, the angled row. Nano Banana 2 (`10` credits, up to 10 reference images) is the default for this compositing. The image prompt describes scene, light, and camera position only - never the interface's contents. Do not name the product, quote its headline, or describe what is on screen; the reference is the source of truth, and describing it is an invitation to redraw it. Inspect the plate at full size before animating: every label legible, screen edges straight, no invented UI elements. Do not spend video credits on a plate that has already drifted.

**Stage 2 - animate the camera.** Feed the plate to video generation and describe motion only.

## Motion budget

The motion prompt is capped at **500 characters**. Order:

1. **Camera** - the one move, its direction, its extent, its speed.
2. **Environment life** - light behavior, reflection, bokeh drift. Sparingly; this shot needs less street life than a billboard.
3. **The lock** - "the screen content stays exactly as it is: it does not change, redraw, animate, or scroll." This clause is never cut, whatever else the character budget costs.

Name the speed as `steady`, `constant`, `natural realtime`. Do not write `slow`, `gentle`, or `soft` - video models literalize those words into slow motion, which reads as heavy and dated on a product shot. (An ambient hero loop wants near-stillness; a fly-through wants one real move at natural speed. Different deliverables, different vocabulary.)

A fly-through wants `4–6` seconds. The move should complete with a beat to spare; a cut-off move reads as an error.

## Model and resolution

| Model | Role | Credits per 5s (480p / 720p / 1080p) |
|---|---|---|
| Seedance Fast | Trial pass - confirm the move and the lock | 15 / 20 / 45 |
| Seedance Pro | The finish default - smoothest camera motion | 25 / 50 / 120 |
| Hailuo | Only when the brand wants visible energy | 30 / 30 / 50 (6s) |

**Always run the trial first: Seedance Fast at 480p, 15 credits.** A trial exists to answer two questions cheaply - does the move land, and does the interface hold? Only then spend on the finish. State the plate cost, the trial cost, and the finish cost together when proposing the shot, and get agreement on the ladder, not on one number: a typical run is `10` (plate) + `15` (trial) + `50` (Seedance Pro 720p finish).

## Prompt skeleton

```text
Steady <orbit right about 12 degrees | push toward the screen | lateral dolly along the row>, one continuous move at constant natural speed, completing with a short hold. <Rim light holds steady | reflections shift subtly on the desk surface | background bokeh drifts>. The screen content stays exactly as it is: it does not change, redraw, animate, or scroll, and every straight edge of the device stays straight. No added text, letters, logos, watermarks, or UI elements. No cursor.
```

Count the characters before sending. If it exceeds 500, cut the environment clause first - never the lock.

## Reject a clip when

- Any label shimmers, re-renders, or grows pseudo-characters. Compare the last frame to the first at full size - drift is progressive, so the last frame is where it shows.
- A straight edge bends: device bezels, screen borders, or card boundaries warping as the camera moves.
- The interface animates - anything scrolls, populates, flips, or lights up that was static in the plate.
- The move overshoots: a `15°` orbit that became `40°`, a push that swallowed the screen edge-to-edge.
- A second move appears - the push that develops a pan, the orbit that starts tilting.
- The screen's glow flickers or the reflection detaches from the device.
- New UI, text, or icons appear anywhere in the scene.
- It only works because nobody looks closely. This asset sits on a launch post; someone will look closely.

Watch it at full size before delivering, and check the last frame against the plate specifically. A clip that survives that comparison is a launch asset; one that does not is a retake, not a note.

---

Shot geometry adapted from [ai-video-generator-claude](https://github.com/rediumvex/ai-video-generator-claude) by @rediumvex, MIT licensed. Camera-only text-survival discipline informed by [krea-marketing](https://github.com/krea-ai/skills) by Krea, MIT licensed.

Rewritten for r3xdec design: built as a two-stage plate-then-animate workflow over the user's own draft screenshot, compressed to the 500-character motion prompt and the model/credit ladder, and the source's live-UI animation guidance ("elements animate, data flows") deliberately inverted into a camera-only lock - on-screen motion is exactly what makes video models redraw an interface.

items.prompt:
OPEN’IX AI
Complete Production-Ready Platform Blueprint & Master Development Prompt
Open’Ix Intelligence OS
AI Chat • Model Hub • Prompt Studio • Knowledge • AI Agents • Workflows
A complete original product specification for planning, designing, building, testing, securing, deploying, and
operating an AI-powered workspace platform.
Design Principle: Build an original Open’Ix product identity and implementation. Reference screenshots may inspire useful
product patterns, but no proprietary branding, logos, or exact layouts should be copied.
Open’Ix AI — Production Blueprint Page 1
1. Executive Product Vision
Open’Ix AI Intelligence OS is a unified AI workspace where users can talk with AI models, manage reusable
prompts, create agents, organize knowledge, experiment with AI, and automate workflows from one connected
platform.
The platform is designed around a shared intelligence layer: authorized workspace and project knowledge can
provide relevant context to AI features without requiring users to repeat important instructions.
Core product flow: User → Workspace → Project → Knowledge & Context → AI Model/Agent → Tools &
Workflows → Results → History & Learning
Production-ready means the system should have clear requirements, validation, testing, observability,
security controls, deployment processes, and rollback plans. No software can honestly promise zero bugs;
the goal is robust engineering and systematic quality assurance.
2. Product Modules
response controls
Transform ideas into structured prompts with templates, versions, categories, testing, and reuse.
Personal and workspace prompt library with folders, tags, favorites, sharing, and lifecycle actions.
Project Knowledge and Workspace Knowledge with sources, permissions, retrieval, versioning, and audit h
Goal-oriented assistants configured with instructions, approved tools, memory policies, knowledge access,
Controlled experiments, prompt/model comparisons, evaluations, datasets, and result tracking.
execution logs.
Module User Value
AI Chat Multi-model conversations with files, authorized knowledge context, conversation history, Model Hub Search, compare, select, configure, and route supported AI providers and models.
Prompt Studio My Prompts Knowledge Hub AI Agents AI Lab Workflows Visual or structured automation using triggers, AI steps, tools, conditions, approvals, and 3. Knowledge Hub — Intelligence Foundation
Project Knowledge belongs to a specific project and can contain purpose, goals, target users, architecture,
APIs, database information, business rules, coding standards, documents, and project-specific AI instructions.
Workspace Knowledge contains reusable rules shared across authorized projects: brand guidelines,
development standards, preferred stack, naming conventions, design principles, language and tone, security
policies, and organizational instructions.
Knowledge pipeline: Source → Validation → Processing → Organization → Permission Check → Retrieval →
Context Assembly → AI Response/Action → Audit
• Manual notes and structured instructions
• Document and file ingestion with source metadata
• Approved website or cloud reference connectors
• Collections, tags, search, source freshness, and version history
• Explicit scope: workspace, project, team, or private
Open’Ix AI — Production Blueprint Page 2
• Role-based permissions and audit records
• Context previews so users can understand what information was used
• Retention and deletion controls for workspace data
4. Workspace and Project Context Rules
The context system should not blindly inject every document into every AI request. It should resolve the active
workspace and project, check permissions, retrieve only relevant material, respect token/context limits, and make
the source scope auditable.
Recommended precedence: Security & platform policy → Organization/workspace rules → Project rules →
Agent configuration → User request. More specific instructions may refine general instructions but must not
bypass higher-priority safety or security controls.
5. AI Chat Experience
• New conversation, rename, archive, search, and history management
• Model selector with provider capabilities and availability states
• Response length, creativity, tone, and tool-use controls
• File attachments and authorized knowledge context
• Streaming responses, cancellation, retry, copy, feedback, and citations where applicable
• Clear loading, empty, error, offline, and rate-limit states
• Desktop, tablet, and mobile responsive layouts
6. AI Agents
An AI Agent is a configurable software assistant that can pursue a user-approved goal through a controlled loop
of understanding, planning, using authorized knowledge and tools, checking results, and returning an outcome.
Agent execution flow: Goal → Context Resolution → Plan → Permission/Policy Check → Tool Execution →
Observation → Next Step → Validation → Result & Log
• Agent identity, purpose, instructions, and personality/tone
• Approved tools and integrations with least-privilege permissions
• Knowledge collections and project/workspace scope
• Memory settings with user-visible controls
• Budgets, timeouts, retries, rate limits, and execution limits
• Human approval gates for consequential external actions
• Run history, logs, outputs, and error reporting
7. Design System
Identity: Premium, calm, futuristic AI workspace. Original Open’Ix visual language with deep charcoal and
midnight surfaces, sophisticated purple and electric-violet accents, soft white typography, subtle borders, and
Open’Ix AI — Production Blueprint Page 3
restrained glass effects.
• Do not reproduce another product's exact layout, logo, illustrations, or distinctive visual identity.
• Use a reusable token system for colors, spacing, typography, radii, shadows, and motion.
• Maintain WCAG-oriented contrast and keyboard-accessible interaction patterns.
• Use responsive breakpoints and touch-friendly controls.
• Provide dark mode first, with a coherent light mode if supported.
8. Recommended Production Architecture
Frontend: Next.js + TypeScript + React + accessible component system + Tailwind CSS or equivalent
token-driven styling.
Backend: A modular API service such as NestJS or FastAPI, with explicit domain boundaries and background
workers for long-running jobs.
Data: PostgreSQL for relational data; Redis for caching/queues where appropriate; object storage for files; a
vector/search system selected according to retrieval requirements.
AI Layer: Provider abstraction, model registry, routing, streaming gateway, tool execution boundary, evaluation,
usage tracking, and graceful provider fallback where product policy permits.
Infrastructure: Containerized services, managed secrets, CI/CD, environment separation, monitoring, backups,
and documented rollback procedures.
9. Core Data Domains
• Identity: users, organizations, workspaces, memberships, roles
• Projects: projects, environments, settings, collaborators
• Knowledge: sources, documents, chunks/indexes, collections, versions, permissions
• AI: providers, models, capabilities, routing policies, usage records
• Chat: conversations, messages, attachments, citations, feedback
• Prompts: prompts, versions, tags, folders, templates, shares
• Agents: definitions, tools, runs, checkpoints, memory policies, approvals
• Workflows: definitions, versions, triggers, runs, steps, logs
• Operations: audit events, notifications, billing/entitlements, support signals
10. API and Service Principles
• Version public APIs and validate all input at trust boundaries.
• Use authentication and authorization checks on every protected resource.
• Prefer idempotency for external actions and background jobs.
• Return structured errors without exposing secrets or internal implementation details.
• Use pagination, filtering, and rate limiting for scalable APIs.
Open’Ix AI — Production Blueprint Page 4
• Document contracts using OpenAPI or equivalent.
11. Security and Privacy Baseline
• Secure authentication, session management, and optional MFA according to product requirements
• Role- and resource-based authorization with tenant/workspace isolation
• Encryption in transit and appropriate encryption at rest
• Secrets stored in a dedicated secret-management system, never hard-coded
• File validation, malware scanning where applicable, and safe content handling
• Audit logs for sensitive administrative and knowledge-access actions
• Dependency scanning, security review, and incident response procedures
• Data export, deletion, and retention controls appropriate to the jurisdictions served
12. Quality Assurance and Testing
• Unit tests for domain logic and critical utilities
• Integration tests for APIs, authorization, database behavior, and provider adapters
• End-to-end tests for primary user journeys
• Accessibility testing and keyboard navigation checks
• Responsive testing across supported viewport categories
• Performance budgets and load testing for critical services
• Failure tests for provider outages, queue failures, invalid files, and partial workflow execution
• Pre-release staging validation and production smoke checks
13. Deployment and Operations
Environment path: Local Development → Automated CI → Preview/Staging → Production
• Separate development, staging, and production configuration
• Automated linting, type checking, tests, and security checks before release
• Database migrations with backups and rollback strategy
• Health checks, structured logs, metrics, tracing, and alerting
• Feature flags for controlled rollout
• Release notes and version tracking
• Incident procedures and documented recovery runbooks
14. Definition of Done
• Feature requirements and acceptance criteria are implemented
• Authorization and validation are reviewed
Open’Ix AI — Production Blueprint Page 5
• Tests cover critical behavior
• Loading, empty, error, and edge states are handled
• Responsive and accessibility checks are completed
• Telemetry and meaningful error logging are present
• Documentation and environment configuration are updated
• Deployment has been tested in a staging-like environment
• Rollback or mitigation approach is documented for meaningful changes
15. Complete Master Build Prompt
You are the product, design, engineering, and quality intelligence layer for Open’Ix AI Intelligence OS. Build
an original, production-oriented AI workspace platform that connects AI Chat, Model Hub, Prompt Studio, My
Prompts, Knowledge Hub, AI Agents, AI Lab, and Workflows. Use Workspace Knowledge as shared context
for authorized projects and Project Knowledge for project-specific context. Never treat knowledge as globally
accessible by default. Resolve scope and permissions before retrieval, retrieve only relevant sources, and
provide auditable context handling. Create a scalable architecture with clear modules, typed contracts,
secure APIs, background processing for long-running jobs, reliable file handling, observability, testing, and
deployment procedures. Prefer maintainable, accessible, responsive components and a consistent
design-token system. Use an original Open’Ix identity: deep charcoal and midnight surfaces with refined
deep-purple and electric-violet accents, soft white typography, subtle borders, and calm futuristic
interactions. Do not copy another company’s branding, logo, proprietary assets, or exact interface layouts.
For every feature: understand the goal, identify requirements and edge cases, design the user flow, define
data and permissions, implement reusable components and services, validate input, handle failures
gracefully, test critical paths, document assumptions, and prepare deployment safely. For AI Agents, use
controlled execution with approved tools, least privilege, budgets, timeouts, run logs, and human approval
gates when external or consequential actions require confirmation. Do not claim software is bug-free.
Instead, use automated testing, reviews, monitoring, staging validation, and rollback readiness to reduce
defects and operate reliably. Deliver implementation-ready specifications, code structures, test plans, and
deployment checklists that a professional engineering team can execute.
16. Suggested Build Roadmap
Phase 1 — Foundation — Identity, workspace/project model, design system, authentication, authorization,
database foundation.
Phase 2 — Core Intelligence — AI Chat, provider abstraction, model registry, conversation history, usage
controls.
Phase 3 — Knowledge — Workspace/Project Knowledge, ingestion, retrieval, permissions, auditability.
Phase 4 — Creation — Prompt Studio, prompt library, templates, versions, testing.
Phase 5 — Agents — Agent builder, tools, knowledge access, runs, approvals, logs.
Phase 6 — Automation — Workflow definitions, triggers, workers, execution history.
Phase 7 — Quality & Operations — Security hardening, evaluations, analytics, monitoring, CI/CD, production
readiness.
Open’Ix AI — Production Blueprint Page 6
Final Product Direction
Open’Ix AI should feel like a connected intelligence workspace rather than a collection of disconnected AI tools.
Knowledge provides context, models provide intelligence, prompts provide reusable intent, agents perform
structured tasks, and workflows connect repeatable processes.
This blueprint is a complete foundation for professional product planning and implementation. Individual
provider APIs, hosting choices, legal/privacy requirements, pricing, and deployment credentials should be
selected and configured during implementation according to the target market and operational needs.

## ⚠️ 强制执行规则（必须严格遵守）

> **本 skill 定义了严格的三阶段分析流程，任何分析任务都必须按照以下步骤执行，不得跳过任何步骤。**
> **详细规则见 [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)**

### 报告生成最佳实践（100页+详细报告）

**并行子代理模式**：将报告分为3部分并行生成，最后合并：
1. 第一部分（~40页）：第一阶段 问题分析（课题信息+课题梳理+功能分析+裁剪+因果链+聚焦关键问题）
2. 第二部分（~40页）：第二阶段 方案产出（11题路由+专利挖掘+矛盾分析+物场分析+功能导向搜索+方案矩阵+ARIZ+方案说明书）
3. 第三部分（~25页）：第三阶段 方案落地 + 附录（实施路线图+原理样件设计+结论+质量自评+格式检查）

**单代理顺序模式**（无子代理时）：每个部分顺序写入临时文件，最后 `cat` 合并：
```bash
# 写入临时文件 part_01.md, part_02.md, ...
# 合并
cat part_01.md part_02.md part_03.md > 完整版.md
# 验证
wc -c 完整版.md && wc -l 完整版.md
# 清理
rm -f part_*.md
```
详细流程见 `references/sequential-report-generation.md`。

**输出格式**：每个报告必须生成3种格式：
- `.md` — 版本控制、在线查看
- `.docx` — 正式提交、打印（使用 `scripts/triz_md_to_docx.py`）
- `.pdf` — 分发、归档（使用 docx2pdf）

**Word 文档生成**：使用 `scripts/triz_md_to_docx.py` 脚本（python-docx），**不要用 pandoc**（无法生成正确目录和封面页）。

```bash
# 基本用法
python scripts/triz_md_to_docx.py input.md output.docx --author "作者名"

# 批量转换
for file in TRIZ_*_完整版.md; do
  python scripts/triz_md_to_docx.py "$file" "${file%.md}.docx" --author "作者名"
done

# 转换为 PDF（需要 docx2pdf）
pip install docx2pdf
python -c "from docx2pdf import convert; convert('report.docx', 'report.pdf')"
```

**Word 文档特性**：
- 封面页（标题+副标题+作者+日期）
- 目录页（三级目录，打开 Word 后右键"更新域"生成）
- 一级标题前自动分页
- 表格样式（深蓝表头白字，交替行颜色）
- 页边距：上下2.54cm，左右3.18cm

## 路径选择网关（统一入口）

每个 TRIZ 分析都从这里开始。判断：**问题边界清晰 + 核心矛盾明确 + 约束已知？**

| 条件 | 推荐路径 | 说明 |
|------|----------|------|
| ✅ 三项都满足 | **放射型 (Radial)** | 全自动分析，一次输入输出完整报告 |
| ❌ 任一项缺失 | **收敛型 (Convergent)** | 多轮对话教练，共同定义问题后转入放射型 |

### 放射型 — TRIZ 分析师

**人格**：静默执行的全自动分析引擎。中间过程零打断，缺失信息用假设填补并标注，只汇报 4 类里程碑通知。

**执行流程**：
```
用户输入 → 问题解析 & 工具路由 → Triz-AI 专利挖掘 → 工具执行 → 融合专利 → 报告
```

### 收敛型 — TRIZ 教练

**人格**：Socratic 式对话者。每次只问一个问题，自然引入 TRIZ 术语，4 阶段收敛：

1. **问题初探**：谁、什么事、为什么 → 能一句话说清场景
2. **TRIZ 深挖**：矛盾识别、IFR 定义 → 矛盾+IFR 都明确
3. **边界收敛**：锁定问题边界 → 用户确认"这就是我要解决的问题"
4. **输出路线图**：问题定义书 + 执行路线图 → 转入放射型执行

用户随时可以说"直接分析"跳转到放射型。

## Pitfalls

### ⚠️ triz-ai 模型名称不能带 `openai/` 前缀

triz-ai 未安装 litellm 时使用原生 OpenAI SDK，会把模型名原样发送到 API。

```yaml
# ❌ 错误 — MiMo API 返回 "Unsupported model openai/mimo-v2.5-pro"
default_model: openai/mimo-v2.5-pro

# ✅ 正确 — 直接用模型 ID
default_model: mimo-v2.5-pro
```

### ⚠️ Embedding 必须单独配置 api_base

不在 `embeddings:` 下指定 `api_base` 会用 LLM 的 api_base（MiMo）请求 embedding，导致失败。Ollama 端点：`http://localhost:11434/v1`。

### ⚠️ Python 版本与 Hermes venv 冲突

运行 triz-ai 前必须：
```bash
export PYTHONPATH="" && export PATH="/c/Users/jianw/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python314:/c/Users/jianw/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python314/Scripts:$PATH"
```

### ⚠️ MiMo API 可用模型

`mimo-v2.5`, `mimo-v2.5-pro`, `mimo-v2.5-asr`, `mimo-v2.5-tts`。不存在 `mimo-v2-pro` 或 `mimo-v2-flash`。

### ⚠️ 报告必须保存为文件

分析完成后，报告必须同时输出到聊天 **AND** 保存为 Markdown 文件。

```bash
# 文件路径格式
~/Documents/TRIZ_创新分析报告_<课题简称>.md
```

使用 `write_file` 工具将完整报告保存到文件，确保用户有持久化副本。不要只在聊天中输出报告而不保存。

### ⚠️ 大文件写入必须分块（防 stream timeout）

单次 `write_file` 超过 ~20KB 会导致 stream timeout（tool call 被截断，文件未写入）。**必须分块写入**：

**分块策略**：
1. **第一块** (`write_file`)：封面+目录+1.1+1.2前半，控制在 ~20KB
2. **后续块** (`patch` mode='patch')：用 `@@ context @@` 锚点追加，每块 ~15-25KB
3. **锚点技巧**：context hint 用上一块最后一行的唯一文本，确保定位准确
4. **验证**：每次写入后用 `terminal` 执行 `wc -l -c file.md` 确认文件增长正常

**第一部分（~40页）推荐分块**：
| 块 | 工具 | 内容 | 预估大小 |
|----|------|------|---------|
| 1 | `write_file` | 封面+目录+1.1课题收集+1.2前半 | ~20KB |
| 2 | `patch` | 1.2后半（MPV+S曲线+IFR+组件+流程+约束） | ~18KB |
| 3 | `patch` | 1.3功能分析（矩阵+功能建模+物场模型） | ~15KB |
| 4 | `patch` | 1.4裁剪+1.5因果链+1.6聚焦+检查清单 | ~20KB |

**错误模式**：直接 `write_file` 写入 40 页完整报告 → stream timeout → 文件为空或不完整。

### ⚠️ 必须严格遵循 AGENTS.md 流程（关键）

用户明确要求：**分析过程必须严格按照 AGENTS.md 定义的流程执行，不得跳过任何步骤。**

常见错误：
1. **跳过路径选择网关** — 必须首先判断放射型/收敛型
2. **跳过11题问题路由** — 第一阶段完成后必须执行
3. **报告过于简略** — 参考 AITRIZ 91页报告标准，每个节点必须有详细输出
4. **只在聊天输出不保存** — 报告必须保存为文件
5. **缺少物理矛盾分析** — 分离原理是四维度TRIZ分析的核心维度之一
6. **缺少物场分析** — Su-Field模型+76标准解是四维度TRIZ分析的核心维度之一
7. **缺少综合解决方案矩阵** — 必须将四个TRIZ维度交叉映射

### ⚠️ Word 生成必须用 python-docx 脚本（关键）

**不要用 pandoc 生成 Word**，pandoc 无法生成正确的三级目录和封面页。

必须使用 `scripts/triz_md_to_docx.py`：
```bash
python scripts/triz_md_to_docx.py input.md output.docx --author "作者名"
```

转换为 PDF：
```bash
pip install docx2pdf
python -c "from docx2pdf import convert; convert('report.docx', 'report.pdf')"
```

详细工作流见 `references/parallel-report-generation.md`。

### ⚠️ Windows/MSYS 路径陷阱（关键）

在 Windows + Git Bash (MSYS) 环境下运行 Python 脚本时，路径格式必须注意：

```bash
# ❌ 错误 — 反斜杠路径被 MSYS 双重转义，导致文件找不到
python "C:\Users\jianw\...\script.py" "C:\Users\jianw\...\input.md"

# ❌ 错误 — MSYS 风格路径在 Python 命令中也会被错误转换
python "/c/Users/jianw/...\script.py"

# ✅ 正确 — 使用正斜杠的 Windows 路径
python "C:/Users/jianw/.../script.py" "C:/Users/jianw/.../input.md" --author "作者名"
```

**根本原因**：MSYS 的路径自动转换 (`MSYS_NO_PATHCONV`) 会把 `/c/...` 转成 `C:\...`，但当路径已经在引号内时，反斜杠可能被二次转义为 `\\`。

### ⚠️ docx2pdf 在 Windows 上需要 Microsoft Word

`docx2pdf` 在 Windows 上依赖 Microsoft Word 进行转换。如果未安装 Word，会报错。替代方案：
```bash
# 使用 LibreOffice
soffice --headless --convert-to pdf report.docx
```

triz-ai 的 `discover` 命令**只接入 CNIPA（中国国家知识产权局）数据库**，结果 100% 为中国专利。对于需要全球视野的课题，必须手动补充国际专利检索。

**补充检索方法**：

| 数据源 | 方法 | 注意事项 |
|--------|------|----------|
| Google Patents | `browser_navigate` 到 `patents.google.com` 搜索 | API 有速率限制（~3次查询后返回503），需用多个子代理并行检索 |
| Espacenet | `patents.epo.org` 搜索 | 可能有 Cloudflare 防护 |
| WIPO PATENTSCOPE | `patentscope.wipo.int` 搜索 | 需注册 |

**推荐检索策略**：
1. 中文关键词 + 英文关键词 + IPC分类号 三管齐下
2. 按主要申请人（Toyota, Samsung SDI, Bosch 等）定向检索
3. 至少覆盖 US/EP/JP/KR 四个地区的专利

**IPC 分类号速查（PCM 热管理相关）**：
- H01M：电池热管理
- B60L：电动车动力系统
- B60H：车辆 HVAC
- F28D：PCM 换热器
- Y02E/Y02T：储能/交通（环保分类）

**输出格式**：国际专利补充分析作为独立报告，与主报告合并参考。

### ⚠️ EPO OPS OAuth2 认证方式（关键）

EPO OPS 使用 **HTTP Basic Auth + OAuth2** 认证，**不能用 `requests.auth` 参数**：

```python
import base64

# ✅ 正确 — 手动构建 Basic 认证头
credentials = f"{consumer_key}:{consumer_secret}"
encoded = base64.b64encode(credentials.encode()).decode()
headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Basic {encoded}",
    "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
}
resp = requests.post(token_url, headers=headers, data={"grant_type": "client_credentials"})

# ❌ 错误 — requests.auth 会导致 401 "Client credentials are invalid"
resp = requests.post(token_url, auth=(consumer_key, consumer_secret), ...)
```

**当前 EPO OPS 配置**（App: jianpatentops, Status: approved）：
```bash
export EPO_CONSUMER_KEY="your_consumer_key"
export EPO_CONSUMER_SECRET="your_consumer_secret"
```

### ⚠️ EPO OPS 返回 expires_in 是字符串（关键）

EPO OPS API 返回的 `expires_in` 是**字符串**而非整数，必须转换：

```python
# ❌ 错误 — TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'float' and 'str'
self.token_expires = time.time() + data.get("expires_in", 3600) - 60

# ✅ 正确
self.token_expires = time.time() + int(data.get("expires_in", 3600)) - 60
```

### ⚠️ CSV 导出必须处理额外字段（关键）

Patent 数据类有 `family_id`, `claims_count`, `description_length`, `compliance_issues`, `citations` 等字段，CSV fieldnames 必须包含或使用 `extrasaction='ignore'`：

```python
# ❌ 错误 — ValueError: dict contains fields not in fieldnames
writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)

# ✅ 正确 — 忽略不在 fieldnames 中的字段
writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames, extrasaction='ignore')

# ✅ 或者 — 在 fieldnames 中包含所有字段
fieldnames = ["patent_id", "title", ..., "family_id", "claims_count", "description_length"]
```

### ⚠️ Google Custom Search API 配置复杂度

Google Custom Search API 需要**三重配置**才能使用：
1. **项目级启用**：Google Cloud Console → API 和服务 → 启用 Custom Search API
2. **计费账户**：某些项目需要关联计费账户
3. **搜索引擎 ID**：在 programmablesearchengine.google.com 创建搜索引擎，获取 cx 参数

**常见陷阱**：
- API Key 在启用 API **之前**创建 → Key 没有新 API 的权限 → 需要重新创建 Key
- 不同项目中的 API Key 无法访问其他项目的 API → 确保 Key 和 API 在同一项目
- 即使显示"已启用"，仍可能返回 403 "project does not have access" → 等待 5-10 分钟或重新创建 Key

**建议**：如果配置困难，直接使用子代理浏览器检索（最可靠）。

- 内联格式支持：**粗体**、`代码`、*斜体*

**关键实现细节**：
```python
# TOC 域代码（必须用 XML 注入）
fldChar1 = parse_xml(f'<w:fldChar {nsdecls("w")} w:fldCharType="begin"/>')
instrText = parse_xml(f'<w:instrText {nsdecls("w")} xml:space="preserve"> TOC \\o "1-3" \\h \\z \\u </w:instrText>')

# 表格样式（深蓝表头）
shading = parse_xml(f'<w:shd {nsdecls("w")} w:fill="003366" w:val="clear"/>')
cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr().append(shading)
```

### ⚠️ Python 类定义中不能在类级别使用 self（关键）

在 Python 类定义中，**类级别的字典/列表不能引用 `self`**，因为 `self` 只在实例方法中可用。

```python
# ❌ 错误 — NameError: name 'self' is not defined
class ComplianceChecker:
    REQUIREMENTS = {
        "check": self._check_method,  # ❌ self 在类级别不可用
    }

# ✅ 正确 — 在 __init__ 中定义
class ComplianceChecker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.REQUIREMENTS = {
            "check": self._check_method,  # ✅ self 在实例方法中可用
        }
```

**此 bug 在 patent_search.py v2.0 中出现过**，已修复。

### ⚠️ 专利检索 API 认证要求（关键）

| API | 认证方式 | 配置方法 | 优先级 |
|-----|----------|----------|--------|
| **Lens.org** | Bearer Token | 注册后获取 API Key，设置 `LENS_API_KEY` | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ |
| **EPO OPS** | OAuth2 | 注册后获取 consumer_key/secret | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ |
| **BigQuery** | Google Cloud | 设置 `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ |
| **PatentsView** | 无需认证 | 直接使用（但 API 格式可能已变更） | ⭐⭐⭐ |
| **Google Patents** | 无需认证 | 直接使用，**速率限制严格**（~3次后503） | ⭐⭐ |

**降级策略**：
1. Lens.org 不可用 → 跳过，使用 EPO
2. EPO 不可用 → 降级到 Google Patents
3. Google Patents 被限流 → 使用 triz-ai 本地数据 + AI 知识
4. 所有 API 都不可用 → 启动子代理通过浏览器手动检索

### ⚠️ 方案辩论系统已集成（v2.0 新增）

TRIZ 报告生成完成后，可自动启动**方案辩论系统**（`solution-debate` skill），通过正反两派对抗性辩论筛选 Top 3 方案。

**触发条件**：报告方案矩阵 ≥ 5 个候选方案时建议启动。

**架构**：四角色模式（正方+反方+裁判+落地分析专家），采用排名稳定性+评分差值混合收敛判定。

**执行流程**：
```
报告完成 → 提取方案矩阵 → Round1辩论(并行) → 收敛检查
  ├── 已收敛 → 裁决+落地分析(并行) → 输出
  └── 未收敛 → Round2交叉反驳 → 收敛检查 → ...（最多3轮）
```

**输出**：Top 3 方案 + 每方案8维度落地分析（市场/竞品/护城河/成本/GTM/路线图/风险/ROI）。

详细规则见 `solution-debate` skill。

### ⚠️ TRIZ 理论学习材料已创建

完整的 TRIZ 理论学习手册已创建：`~/Documents/TRIZ_理论学习手册.md`

**内容**：13 章 + 3 个附录，覆盖所有 TRIZ 工具的原理、方法和评价标准，每个工具配有简单示例。

**可用于**：生成培训材料、回答 TRIZ 理论问题、指导初学者学习。

items.title: Hero Overlap Thin Bridge Strip
items.description: Creates a full-window hero for Impact Minds with a very thin floating overlap strip that replaces the current strip below the hero. The strip bridges the hero and the next section and includes a premium insurance CTA.
items.prompt:
SKILL NAME:
Hero Overlap Thin Bridge Strip

SHORT DESCRIPTION:
Creates a full-window hero for Impact Minds with a very thin floating overlap strip that replaces the current strip below the hero. The strip bridges the hero and the next section and includes a premium insurance CTA.

PROMPT:
Create a premium hero layout system for Impact Minds that uses a very thin floating overlap strip in place of the current strip below the hero.

This skill is for REPLACING the existing strip only.

Do NOT create a new block.
Do NOT add a second container.
Do NOT build a new section.
Do NOT duplicate the current strip.
Only replace the current strip with a refined overlap bridge strip.

HERO RULES
- Hero image or hero animation must fill the full visible browser window
- Hero must feel full-screen and cinematic
- Hero must NOT exceed visible window parameters
- Hero height must stay locked to the viewport so nothing important is pushed below the fold
- All core hero content must remain visible inside the viewport
- Maintain contained content width inside the hero
- Use a cinematic premium image with a soft overlay for readability
- Keep the hero calm, minimal, editorial, and premium
- Do not let the hero become taller than the screen
- Do not let hero content extend outside the first visible screen

HERO CONTENT
- Page label at top left above hero content
- Headline
- Subheadline
- CTA buttons
- Micro reassurance line

HEADLINE TYPOGRAPHY
- First half of headline: Roboto Bold
- Second half of headline: Roboto Italic
- Split across 2 lines
- Clear visual hierarchy between the two lines
- First line should feel like the anchor
- Second line should feel like the softer editorial continuation

OVERLAP STRIP SYSTEM
- Replace the current strip below the hero with a single thin floating overlap strip
- The strip must overlap the bottom of the hero image and the top of the next section
- 50% of the strip should cover the hero image
- 50% of the strip should sit inside the next section below
- The strip should act as a bridge between the hero and the next block
- Do NOT place the strip fully inside the hero
- Do NOT place the strip fully below the hero
- Do NOT create extra stacked content
- Do NOT turn it into a large card
- It must remain as thin as possible

SIZE AND PLACEMENT
- Total strip height must be 80px
- Keep the strip horizontally centered inside the page container
- The strip should not be full width
- Width should feel premium and intentional, approximately 70% to 85% of the main content container
- Add enough spacing below hero content so the strip does not collide with hero text or buttons
- The strip should feel like a light editorial bridge, not a bulky CTA block

CONTENT RULES
- All strip content and the CTA button must fit on a SINGLE LINE
- No stacked text
- No wrapped text
- No second row
- No section label needed
- No card subtitle above the content
- Keep copy minimal, clear, and premium
- Include one short support line on the left
- Include one single CTA button on the right

CTA RULE
- Use only ONE CTA button in the strip
- CTA should be insurance-focused
- Button text: Verify Insurance
- Make the insurance CTA feel premium, highly legible, and visually clear
- CTA should feel calm and confidence-building, not aggressive

LAYOUT
- Horizontal layout only
- Text aligned on the left
- Single CTA aligned on the right
- Everything vertically centered
- Maintain clean spacing between the text and the button
- Keep the strip elegant, slim, and visually quiet
- Avoid crowding

VISUAL STYLE
- Premium floating strip feel
- Rounded corners: 20px–24px
- Soft elevation
- Subtle shadow
- Light neutral background
- Cohesive with the hero image and next section
- No clutter
- No heavy borders
- No dark or harsh framing
- No black text
- Text colors: #7F776F or #2A2A2A only
- Primary CTA button color: #7F776F
- CTA text must remain high contrast and legible
- The strip should feel soft, editorial, and premium

MOTION
- Hero image should have subtle motion such as slow parallax or slow zoom
- The overlap strip can fade in softly
- The strip may have slight upward motion on reveal
- The CTA button may have a subtle hover lift
- Motion must be minimal, refined, and calm
- No flashy animation
- No bounce effects

SPACING AND STRUCTURE
- Maintain generous page margins
- Keep hero content inside the main content container
- Make sure the overlap strip does not block key hero content
- Keep the transition from hero to next section seamless and layered
- Ensure the strip feels integrated into the layout, not pasted on top of it

FINAL GOAL
- The result should feel like a premium editorial hero system with a very thin overlap bridge strip
- The strip should replace the current strip, not add a new one
- The strip should create depth without bulk
- The strip should improve conversion with a calm premium insurance CTA
- The overall effect should feel clean, structured, minimal, and intentional

items.title: Image Generation / Hero Visual
items.description: Generate a landing-page hero visual that HTML text sits on top of - abstract field, object study, or environment, with no text baked into the pixels. Enforces a text safe zone and a contrast budget for overlay legibility. Informed by ConardLi's gpt-image-2 skill (MIT).
items.prompt:
# Hero Visual

Generate the hero *image*, never the hero *section*. The headline, subhead, and CTA are real HTML that sits on top of this image. Any text baked into the pixels is a defect: it cannot be edited, translated, selected, or read by a screen reader, and it will not survive a copy change.

## When to use

- The user asks for a hero image, key visual, above-the-fold background, or section imagery for a landing page.
- A generated page has a hero block that is currently a flat color or a placeholder and needs a real visual.
- The user asks for a background for a CTA band, feature section, pricing header, or footer.

Do not use for: a mascot or app icon (use `Image Generation / IP as Logo`), a UI screenshot or device mockup, an infographic, or a diagram.

## Ask before generating, in this order

Ask only for what you cannot infer from the project's existing design drafts, brand guide, or copy. Never run more than one round of questions.

1. What the section says — the actual headline, so the visual can support it rather than fight it. Use it to size and place the quiet zone, and for nothing else. Never put the headline, subhead, CTA label, or brand name into the image prompt — not as a quotation, not as an example, not as an explanation of what the zone is reserved for. Naming the copy in the prompt is the single most reliable way to get it rendered into the pixels, and it defeats every negative constraint you write afterwards.
2. Where the text sits — left column, centered, or bottom overlay. This decides the safe zone.
3. Brand colors, if the project does not already define them.
4. Aspect ratio, if the section is not a standard full-bleed hero.

## Pick one of three routes

Commit to a single route per candidate. Mixing routes is what produces generic stock-art slop.

**Abstract field** — gradient meshes, soft light, glass, grain, flowing geometry. The safest default: it never competes with the copy, reads well at any crop, and survives dark mode. Use when the product is abstract (infra, AI, fintech, dev tools) or when the copy must dominate.

**Object study** — one hero object rendered cleanly on a simple ground: the product, a symbolic artifact, or a stylized 3D form. Use when there is one concrete thing to show. Exactly one object, no scene, no props.

**Environment** — a real or stylized space that the product lives in: a workspace, a storefront, a landscape. Use for lifestyle, travel, commerce, and hospitality. The highest-risk route: it dates fastest and most easily reads as stock photography.

## Composition and the safe zone

- Default to `21:9` for a full-bleed hero band, `16:9` for a standard hero, `4:3` or `1:1` for a side-by-side hero where the visual occupies one column.
- Reserve the text region as deliberately empty, low-detail, low-contrast space. For a left-aligned hero, keep the left `40–45%` quiet and push the visual weight right. For a centered hero, keep the middle third quiet and let interest live at the edges.
- State the safe zone in the prompt as pure geometry and tone: "keep the left 45% quiet, flat, and low-detail". Do not tell the image model what will go there, and do not use the word "text" outside the constraints line. "A reserved text zone for the headline …" is how a headline ends up rendered in the image.
- Keep the focal element off-center and away from the exact middle unless the layout is centered.
- Do not compose to the edges of the frame. The image will be cropped differently at mobile, tablet, and desktop; anything meaningful within `8%` of any edge will be lost.
- Never build a frame, border, rounded card, browser chrome, or device bezel into the image. The layout provides those.

## Contrast budget

The overlay text has to pass contrast against whatever pixel it lands on. Decide the text color first, then constrain the image to serve it.

- For light text: hold the safe zone in the darker half of the range and forbid bright highlights, blown-out areas, and white glow inside it.
- For dark text: hold the safe zone light and even, and forbid dark objects, deep shadows, and heavy vignettes inside it.
- Keep the safe zone tonally *flat*, not merely dark or light. A busy region at the right average brightness still destroys legibility.
- If the design calls for a scrim, say so as a layout decision and keep it in CSS. Do not bake a gradient overlay into the image.

## Color

- Pull from the project's existing palette. A hero visual that introduces a fourth brand color is a defect, not a variation.
- Use the brand color as the dominant field or the accent, not both.
- Keep the whole image inside one temperature family unless the brand is explicitly high-contrast.
- Generate for the project's default theme first. If the page supports dark mode, expect to generate a second variant rather than hoping one image works in both.

## Prompt skeleton

```text
Create one <aspect ratio> hero visual for a <product category> landing page. This is a background image only; all text is added separately in HTML.
Route: <abstract field | object study | environment>.
Subject: <one sentence — the single thing in frame, or the character of the abstract field>.
Composition: keep the <left 45% | middle third | lower third> visually quiet, flat, and low-detail, with no focal element in it. Place visual weight in the <opposite region>. Keep all meaningful content away from the outer 8% of the frame.
Tone: hold that quiet region consistently <dark and even | light and even> across its full width, with no bright spots or tonal jumps inside it.
Color: build from <brand color> as the <dominant field | single accent>, with <supporting neutral>. Stay in one temperature family.
Finish: <material and light description — e.g. soft diffuse light, fine grain, matte surfaces>.
Constraints: Add no text, letters, numbers, watermarks, or logos. Add no frames, borders, rounded corners, cards, browser chrome, or device bezels. Add no user-interface elements, buttons, or cursors. Keep the quiet region free of high-contrast detail, bright highlights, and hard edges. Include no people's faces unless explicitly requested. Do not compose as a collage, grid, or multi-panel image.
```

## Generate and evaluate

Propose two or three routes in one line each, state the credit cost, and generate only after the user picks. Generate one image per call through r3xdec design's built-in image generation.

Before sending, re-read the assembled prompt once and strip it of the product's own words: the headline, subhead, CTA label, and brand name must not appear anywhere, in any form. If the word "text" appears outside the constraints line, rewrite that sentence in terms of geometry and tone. This check costs nothing and prevents the most common failure below.

Reject a candidate when:

- Any text, letterform, digit, or logo appears in the image. This is the most common failure and it almost always traces back to the copy being named in the prompt; fix the prompt, not the image.
- The quiet region contains high-contrast detail, a bright highlight, or a hard edge that will cut through overlay text.
- The focal element sits dead center under a left-aligned or centered headline.
- Meaningful content touches the outer `8%` and will be lost at a narrower crop.
- A frame, border, card, or device bezel is baked in.
- It reads as stock photography: generic smiling people, handshake, lightbulb, rocket, glowing brain, floating holographic UI.
- It introduces a color outside the project's palette.
- The composition is symmetric and centered when the layout is not.

Always place the winning candidate into the actual hero block and view the rendered page before calling it done. A hero visual can only be judged with the real headline sitting on it.

---

Structure informed by [gpt-image-2](https://github.com/ConardLi/garden-skills) from ConardLi's garden-skills, MIT licensed.

Rewritten for r3xdec design: HTML-first hero sections where all copy stays in the DOM, a quiet-region rule that keeps the product's own words out of the image prompt, a contrast budget for overlay legibility, three explicit visual routes, and generation through the built-in image generation.

items.title: Triz-AI CLI — Pitfalls & Configuration Guide
items.description: ## Python Version Conflict (Critical)
items.prompt:
# Triz-AI CLI — Pitfalls & Configuration Guide

## Python Version Conflict (Critical)

triz-ai requires Python >=3.12. Current system has Python 3.11.15 as default.

**Problem**: Running `triz-ai` without path override causes `pydantic_core` import error because Hermes venv (Python 3.11) pollutes `sys.path`.

**Solution**: Always use this prefix before any `triz-ai` command:
```bash
export PYTHONPATH="" && export PATH="/c/Users/jianw/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python314:/c/Users/jianw/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python314/Scripts:$PATH"
```

**Install location**: `C:\Users\jianw\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python314\Scripts\triz-ai.exe`

---

## Model Name Format (Critical)

triz-ai uses raw OpenAI SDK (not litellm). Model names are sent **as-is** to the API endpoint.

```yaml
# ❌ WRONG — MiMo API returns "Unsupported model openai/mimo-v2.5-pro"
default_model: openai/mimo-v2.5-pro

# ✅ CORRECT — direct model ID
default_model: mimo-v2.5-pro
```

The `provider/model` prefix format only works with `pip install triz-ai[litellm]`.

---

## Embedding API Base (Critical)

If `embeddings.api_base` is not set separately, triz-ai uses `llm.api_base` (MiMo) for embeddings, which fails because MiMo doesn't have embedding models.

```yaml
embeddings:
  model: nomic-embed-text
  dimensions: 768
  api_base: http://localhost:11434/v1  # Ollama endpoint
  api_key: ollama                       # Ollama doesn't validate keys
```

---

## MiMo API Available Models

As of 2026-07-22, MiMo API (`https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1/models`) supports:
- `mimo-v2.5` — standard model (use for classify_model)
- `mimo-v2.5-pro` — advanced model (use for default_model, deep_model)
- `mimo-v2.5-asr` — speech recognition
- `mimo-v2.5-tts` — text-to-speech

There is NO `mimo-v2-pro` or `mimo-v2-flash` — those names don't exist.

---

## Environment Variable Interpolation

Config supports `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` syntax. If a variable is unset and no default is provided, triz-ai raises `ConfigError`.

**Workaround**: Either:
1. Create `~/.triz-ai/.env` with the variables
2. Hardcode the API key in config.yaml
3. Use `${VAR:-}` for optional fields

---

## Working Config (2026-07-22)

```yaml
# ~/.triz-ai/config.yaml
llm:
  default_model: mimo-v2.5-pro
  classify_model: mimo-v2.5
  deep_model: mimo-v2.5-pro
  reasoning_effort: medium
  api_base: https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1
  api_key: <from ~/.hermes/.env XIAOMI_API_KEY>

embeddings:
  model: nomic-embed-text
  dimensions: 768
  api_base: http://localhost:11434/v1
  api_key: ollama

database:
  path: ~/.triz-ai/patents.db
```

---

## Ollama Models Installed

- `nomic-embed-text:latest` — 274 MB (embedding, required for triz-ai)
- `qwen2.5vl:3b` — 3.2 GB (vision-language)
- `deepseek-coder:1.3b` — 776 MB (code)

For local LLM analysis, consider installing `ollama pull qwen2.5:7b`.
